slides.texte_overlay:
How to handle criticism
like a grown man
Let them finish before you answer. Interrupting to defend yourself makes it look like the criticism hit a nerve. Hear the whole point first, then respond calmly.
Say thank you, even if it stings. "Thanks for telling me." It costs nothing and shows you're secure enough to hear hard things without falling apart.
Separate the message from the tone. Sometimes useful feedback is delivered badly. Take the part that helps you and quietly let go of the way it was said.
Ask one clarifying question. "Can you give me an example?" It turns vague criticism into something you can actually fix, and shows you take it seriously.
Build a steady mind. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a curious, settled head makes it much easier to hear criticism without panicking.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A curious, settled head makes criticism much easier to hear.

slides.texte_overlay: Sleep on it before you decide. Your first reaction is emotional. The next day, you'll see clearly which parts were fair and which ones weren't.
Show the change. The best answer to criticism is quietly doing better next time. People remember the man who listened and improved, not the one who argued.
